_note: Intra-Near-Eastern blend (Ethiopian + Mesopotamian): a South-Arabian / Sabaean incense kingdom of the desert-mountains. Backbone = Ge'ez/South-Semitic (phonology, amba/debr features, the mlk root); overlay = Akkadian (an astral cult of sun, moon, and the dawn-star; -u endings; mar-filiation; ziggurat-temple flavor). South-Arabian rank titles (Mukarrib, Qayl, Malik) are the real Sabaic register (allowed, catalog 5.3). civ = feudal. Even split Lawful/Neutral. DEITY names are SECOND-ORDER phoneme-morphs: the Agrippan canon as morphed into Punic (Barcan) trade-forms, then drifted again through South-Semitic phonology — the shared Punic-cognate ancestor of the family; never real South-Arabian gods.

phonology.palette: Ge'ez/South-Semitic backbone (emphatics t'/s'/q'; gutturals h/h./kh/'; -a endings; triconsonantal roots) with Akkadian overlay touches (-u/-tu endings on some names, mar-filiation); theophoric stems are second-order morphs of the Punic forms (Talrish-, Arganu-, Warlanu-, Riyalat-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; emphatics and gutturals frequent; gemination; the South-Arabian particle dhu- (he of); stress varies.

morphology.patronymic_form: patronymic 'bin-X' (son of) or the South-Arabian 'dhu-X' (he of [clan/house]); Ge'ez 'walda-X' and Akkadian 'mar-X' as secondary forms; theophoric given names on morphed god-stems; nobles a bet/clan house.
morphology.compounding_rule: construct: Beta-[deity] (house of), Mahram-[deity] (sacred-precinct of), Bir-[name] (well of); dhu-[clan] (he of); resource + feature: Bir-Lubban (incense-well).

title_ladder.government: feudal (South-Arabian backbone; the federator priest-kingship and qayl clan-assemblies are narrative flavor, with Ge'ez Ras and Akkadian astral-temple offices as overlay color)
title_ladder._tiers_note: South-Arabian/Sabaic backbone, ascending, on the shared mlk root: Malik/Mamlakat (king/kingdom), Malik-Malikan (king of kings) over the Mamlakat-Kubra. Kabir (chief) barony; Maqtawi (warden-officer) march; Qayl (clan-prince) county; Mukarrib (federator priest-prince) principality. Ge'ez overlay: the highland duchy is styled Ras (head). (Rank titles are the real Sabaic/Ge'ez register, allowed.)

people_name_convention.order: given (often theophoric) + dhu-clan or bin-X patronymic; the renowned earn a caravan/deed epithet.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the qayl nobility carry a dhu-clan name; commoners a bin-patronymic.
people_name_convention.theophoric: given names from the morphed deity-names + a Semitic element: Abd-X (servant-of), Wahab-X (gift-of), Amat-X (handmaid-of, f), or the Ge'ez Walda-X overlay. e.g. Abd-Talrish, Wahab-Arganu, Amat-Riyalat.

religion._note: Deity-names are second-order phoneme-morphs: the canonical Agrippan pantheon as morphed into Punic (Barcan) trade-forms, then drifted through South-Semitic (Ge'ez-kin) phonology with an Akkadian astral coloring — never real South-Arabian gods. Lawful/Neutral; an incense-temple and astral cult (the sun-power, the moon as His lamp, and the dawn-star) layered over saint/ancestor veneration.
religion.the_one: Atyaran (< Punic Atharon < Aeternus; God Most High, lord of the high heaven)
religion.demon_epithet_pattern: each opposing power (the Chaotic 13 for this Lawful-leaning realm) keeps its morphed name + its own portfolio epithet (distinct per power): Maraxus -> Marakash the Devourer; Lusanto -> Lusantan the Coin-Serpent; Vacidus -> Wakidan the Void.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Bet (temple) or Mahram (sacred precinct) of [power]: 'the Mahram of Talrish'.
religion.saints_pattern: the blessed dead and incense-lords, venerated at the Mahram and at pillar-tombs; 'the blessed [name]'.

holy_symbol_motifs.Talrish: a sun-disc between a crescent moon and the dawn-star

banks_patterns.ships: incense-caravan and Red-Sea trader names: 'Bringer of Lubban', 'Star of the Bahr', 'the Crescent of Saba'
banks_patterns.military_units: the [clan] Spears / the [god] Host: 'the Host of Warlanu'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: ruined mahram-precincts and dam-cities of the desert: 'the Mahram of [name]', 'the Sunken Bir of [name]'
